question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}{{f}^{″}({x}_{n})},
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ and ${f}^{″}({x}_{n})$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n},$ respectively.

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2})+{x}^{3})^{′} \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})+3{x}^{2}, \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =(2x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})+3{x}^{2})^{′} \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})-4{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2})+6x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{2{x}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{n}^{2})+3{x}_{n}^{2}}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{n}^{2})-4{x}_{n}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{n}^{2})+6{x}_{n}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=-1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{2{x}_{0}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{0}^{2})+3{x}_{0}^{2}}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{0}^{2})-4{x}_{0}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{0}^{2})+6{x}_{0}} \\  & =-1-\frac{2(-1)\operatorname{cos}⁡((-1)^{2})+3(-1)^{2}}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡((-1)^{2})-4(-1)^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡((-1)^{2})+6(-1)} \\  & =-1+\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-3}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(1)-6} \\  & ≈-0.768,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
